one_liner: Senior federal contracting officer-track role at NTSB: planning, soliciting, negotiating, awarding and administering contracts under the FAR for the agency's Acquisition Division.
fit_summary: This GS-14 1102 job requires at least four years of contracting experience, a year at GS-13 running the full contract lifecycle, 24 semester hours in business fields, and FAC-C Professional. Daniel's procurement and proposal work at IEM was on the contractor side (buying medical supplies, writing bids), not contracting-officer work, so he won't meet the minimum qualifications.
eligibility: Open to the public via Direct Hire (also fed-transition); no federal status or veterans' preference needed.

Basic requirement: at least 4 years in contracting or related positions, including 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-13 (full lifecycle contracting, expert guidance, policy interpretation, contractor evaluations).

Education: a bachelor's degree with at least 24 semester hours in accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management. A transcript is required at application, and there is no education substitution.
Certification: FAC-C Professional or equivalent is required (a waiver by the senior procurement executive is possible but discretionary).
Confidential security clearance required; position is in Washington, DC with telework eligibility.
keywords: Justifications of Other than Full and Open Competition (JOFOCs)
strategy: First audit honestly: list every IEM task where you planned, priced, negotiated or administered contracts or subcontracts. If the total is not 4+ years, with 1 year at an expert level, skip this one and target GS-1102 trainee/GS-7-9 roles or emergency-management/program analyst jobs instead.

If he applies, frame his proposal work as contracting knowledge: researching opportunities on SAM.gov, GovWin and DHS forecasts, reading solicitations and leading proposal writing (2019 to 2024), plus purchasing medical supplies for vaccination sites. Say plainly that it was contractor-side.
Pull your transcript now and count the semester hours in the qualifying fields. Upload it, because the posting will mark you ineligible without it.
Fit everything into the two-page resume limit: state dates, hours per week, and the specialized-experience language plainly. HR says it 'will not make assumptions.'
Answer the questionnaire truthfully, since overstating can remove you. Plan to complete USA Hire within 48 hours after the November 2, 2026 close.

Consider a longer-term path: entry-level 1102 roles open to all U.S. citizens, such as agency acquisition intern or contract specialist trainee postings, would let him earn FAC-C and build on his vendor and proposal work.
resume_bullets: Found multimillion-dollar opportunities in SAM.gov, GovWin, BidPro and the DHS acquisition forecast, and led proposal writing (2019–2024).
As part of the logistics team, procured medical supplies, equipment and vaccines for COVID-19 sites in six states and set up vendor relationships (2021–2022).
interview_questions: Walk us through how you'd plan an acquisition from market research to award, including when a JOFOC is needed.
Describe a time you performed cost or price analysis and how it shaped a negotiation.
How do you advise technical staff whose SOW or requirements are unclear or noncompliant?
Tell us about a contractor performance problem you anticipated and how you resolved it.
watch_outs: The degree hours, 4+ years of contracting experience, and FAC-C requirements are hard gates; without them you will be rated ineligible.
Short window: open October 20 to November 2, 2026, with USA Hire due 48 hours after closing.
A Confidential clearance is required, and the role has no promotion potential above GS-14.
